study type: Secondary cohort analysis of a cluster-randomized trial
exposure: Prenatal physical activity level (adhering to recommendations vs. inactive)
cohort: Pregnant women (n=1994) participating in the GeliS ('healthy living in pregnancy') trial
finding: Prenatal physical activity adherence was associated with higher birth weight, while sedentary behavior was associated with lower birth weight and increased odds of low birth weight.
mod_finding: Light-intensity physical activity in early pregnancy was marginally associated with increased odds of caesarean section.
